housing: Plymouth's private rented sector is concentrated in the Victorian terraces close to the centre, especially in Mutley, Greenbank and North Hill, where many homes are let to University of Plymouth students. Stonehouse and Stoke have Georgian and Victorian terraces split into flats, and Devonport and Keyham have dockyard-era terraces, with large regeneration schemes in Devonport. The waterfront has converted warehouses and new apartment blocks, while Plymstock, Plympton and Estover are mostly post-war and later suburban estates. Many homes face exposure to wind and rain off the Sound.
checkinTips: Student houses in Mutley and Greenbank: photograph each bedroom lock, fire doors, alarms and the shared kitchen and bathroom separately.
Exposed homes facing the Sound and on the hills: record damp and mould, salt marks on windows and rust on railings and fittings.
Flats in Stonehouse and Stoke's split Victorian houses: note communal hallways, meter cupboards, fire doors and the key count.
Waterfront apartments in the Barbican and Royal William Yard: note fob counts, parking bays, balconies and any listed-building features.
Hillside terraces: photograph steps, retaining walls, gutters and the state of rear lanes and yards.
New-build homes in Sherford: record snagging marks, sealant and new turf, fences and parking.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in privately rented homes to Plymouth City Council's private sector housing team.
